text:
matt: heads-up — started seeing persistent GPU resident growth on dedicated pool after yesterday's kernel-picker + batching tweak. looks like memory doesn't drop between requests anymore

sara: ugh. seen any OOMs or just resident creep?

matt: no OOMs yet, but steady +1.2GB/hr on a p3.8xlarge replica serving chat workloads. KV cache size in metrics also creeps up, but traces show many small allocations from workspace allocator after kernel change

kai: can you paste the diff for the kernel picker change? maybe the fallback path allocates different workspace sizes

matt: pasted below — only ~6 lines changed. main change: prefer fused-gemm-kernel when sequence_len < 1024, otherwise runtime picks generic-kernel. also changed batching heuristic to more aggressive pack_within_200ms

```diff
- select_kernel(seq_len) -> generic if seq_len > 512
+ select_kernel(seq_len) -> fused_gemm if seq_len < 1024
+ batch_window_ms = 200
```

lucy: hmm, fused_gemm reduces FLOPs but it needs a larger workspace buffer for precomputed transposes. if allocator is suboptimal that could fragment and fail to reuse older buffers

matt: repro script attached (quick local): repro_small_workload.py — spins requests with varying seq_len 256/768 in 70/30 ratio. when fused_gemm chosen, resident climbs. with generic-only, stable.

repro-bot: repro run summary (short):
- 30m run, steady-state request QPS=60
- fused_gemm path: +18% resident over baseline, KV-cache nominal +12%
- generic path: stable

kai: can you run profiler snapshot (cuda-mem-snapshot) and allocator-stats at t=0, t=30m, t=60m? want to see free lists and slab occupancy

matt: pasted important bits from allocator-stats:

"""
allocator: total_allocated=27.4GB
slab: 8 slabs (4MB each) active
free_list_small: counts -> 0,0,2,1
workspace_holder: recent_allocs: 1.4MB x 1200 entries
KV-cache: entries=12452, resident=6.3GB
"""

lucy: that "workspace_holder recent_allocs" looks suspect — hundreds of ~1MB entries. should be pooled not kept per-request. what does kernel runtime request pattern look like?

matt: runtime trace: each seq with fused_gemm calls allocate_workspace(1MB) then enqueue kernel; free called only after batch completion. with aggressive batching, batches coalesce and the free happens but allocator seems to create fresh slab segments instead of reusing because the requested alignment differs (256 vs 512)

sara: alignment mismatch. maybe fused_gemm asks for 256-byte aligned transposed buffer which our old allocator treated as small allocation and put in different freelist. recent change to rounding rules could have split the bin boundaries

kai: can we try two quick experiments on a staging replica: 1) force kernel picker to generic, 2) keep fused_gemm but normalize workspace requests to 512 alignment in kernel code. measure resident delta after 30m

matt: running both now. experiment ids: exp-196A (generic forced), exp-196B (align->512). I'll drop results in 35m

(35m later)

matt: exp-196A (generic) -> stable resident. exp-196B (align512) -> small initial bump then flat after 10m. looks like alignment fix fixes reuse.

lucy: good signal. alignment change means allocator can reuse existing slabs instead of allocating new ones for slightly different sizes. this was likely a regression when we tightened rounding in allocator tuning PR #4521

sara: can we push alignment normalization for fused_gemm workspace and revert the packing window tweak? or maybe set pack_within_ms to 120 while we validate

kai: also add diagnostic counters: workspace_alloc_requests, workspace_reuse_hits, workspace_frag_bytes sampled per minute. that'll help detect regressions early

matt: filing a small rollback/patch:
- revert batching window -> 120ms
- add alignment normalization: workspace_request_align = 512
- emit allocator counters perf/metrics

eng-oncall: tagging incident rotation. no customer-visible OOMs but this had capacity impact. please post deploy plan and rollout cadence

matt: deploying patch to dedicated pool canary -> 2 replicas now, will expand to 20% if resident stable for 1 hour

lucy: follow-up: we should add a unit test that asserts workspace allocations of varying sizes reuse same slab bins (simulate align rounding). also add a small fuzz harness that flips kernel choices to ensure allocator remains stable

sara: also check KV-cache eviction heuristics: if workspace reuse stalls, we might incorrectly retain KV entries because eviction only triggers under alloc failure, not allocation growth. add a soft-evict trigger on steady resident increase

kai: agreed. i'll open two follow-ups: #alloc-alignment-fix (hotfix) and #kv-soft-evict (postmortem follow-up)

matt: patch rolled out to 20% -> resident flat at 20% nodes after 40m. expanding to 100% now. will monitor overlays and send final summary in morning

lucy: nice detective work. lesson: kernel selection + batching interacts subtly with allocator alignment and freelist boundaries. document in perf-runbook (allocator gotcha section)

sara: adding notes to runbook and creating a dashboard for workspace_reuse_rate

matt: final note: repro script + profiler snapshots saved in s3://redwood-perf/leak-investigations/1961122334/ — contains nvprof, allocator dumps, and the small repro harness

repro-bot: archived run artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/leak-investigations/1961122334/artifacts.tar.gz :thumbsup:

matt: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem writeup is in #postmortems

eng-oncall: :white_check_mark:
